To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the discontinuous horizontal representation in V2d is maintained by long-range horizontal connections with V1, V2v, and extrastriate visual areas; (2) the V2d representation of the horizontal meridan (HM) can be maintained by long-range connections with V2d and V2v; and (3) V2d neurons that are located near the V2 rostrocaudal border can maintain the representation of the HM by making connections with

the discontinuous representation of the horizontal meridan (HM) in primate area V-2 (V-2d and V-2v) is maintained by connections between the two halves of this area, as well as by connections with other visual areas.

V2d neurons make nonretinotropic horizontal connections with neurons representing the lower visual quadrant in the infragranular and supragranular layers of V2v, as well as with neurons representing the upper visual field in the infragraynarular layers of extrastriatal visual cortex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural representation of space in the primate visual system.
the anatomical organization of the primate visual cortex and the role of this organization in the visual perception of form and motion.
how visual field continuity is maintained within the second-order discontinuous representation of the primate visual cortex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the discontinuous topographic representation in V2 is a result of the anatomical organization of this area and not of the visual system as a whole.

the anatomical evidence for classical RF completion across the discontinuity of the V2 HM representation is provided by local and long-range connections with V2 neurons representing the upper visual quadrants and that this is achieved by a combination of retinotopic and nonretinotopy connections.

the V2d and V2v representations are not truly discontinuous, but are connected by long-range horizontal connections that extend across the HM representation, allowing the V2d representation to be completed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there are two types of discontinuities in V2: (1) a discontinuity of the visual field representation at the rostral V2 border and (2) a discontinuity in the connectional field of V2 at the rostral border.
the visual cortex is a mosaic of discontinuous topographical representations that can be connected to form a continuous perceptual representation.

the discontinuous topography in V2 is not the result of a simple "split" of the V1 representation, but rather is the result of an intricate pattern of local and long-range connections that maintain retinotopical and perceptual continuity within V2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the visual field can be represented discontinuously within a single visual area, but that this discontinuity is bridged by interhemispheric, intra-areal, and extrastriate cortical connections.

, although there is a discontinuity of the horizontal meridians representation in area V2 (i.e. the representation of the lower visual quadrant in V2d and the representation of the upper visual quadrant in V 2v), there is still a visual field continuity across these representations.
the visual cortex of primates is a complex network of interconnected cortical regions that work together to process visual information.
